acceptance.given: The compiled obligation graph contains Atomic Obligation nodes and assertion nodes with declared coverage links.

oracle.expected: The exact-cover validator emits a report proving forward coverage from every Atomic Obligation to assertions and reverse coverage from every assertion node to its corresponding Atomic Obligation, with no orphan nodes.
forbidden: Any Atomic Obligation is covered in only one direction.
Any assertion node lacks corresponding Atomic Obligation coverage.
The report omits forward or reverse coverage.
oracle.observable: Structured validator output containing complete forward and reverse Atomic Obligation-to-assertion mappings and zero orphan nodes.

acceptance.then: The validation report records mutually complete forward and reverse coverage for every Atomic Obligation-to-assertion relationship and identifies no orphan node.
acceptance.when: Run the repository exact-cover validator against the compiled obligation graph and evaluate its emitted coverage artifact.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select a graph with at least one Atomic Obligation-to-assertion link missing in the forward or reverse direction and verify that exact-cover validation rejects it.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Ensure exact-cover validation checks both directions for every Atomic Obligation-to-assertion relationship, rejects orphan nodes, and emits an observable forward/reverse coverage report. This Governance constraint requires structural validation rather than an expected-red runtime marker.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Revert only exact-cover validator and regression-test changes; no persisted state or schema migration is altered.

slice_hint.state_transition: Unverified bidirectional coverage -> validator examines graph -> exact cover is proven or deterministic rejection identifies the missing direction.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Validation emits forward and reverse coverage for every Atomic Obligation-to-assertion pair with zero orphans; malformed one-way coverage deterministically fails.
